newsitem.title: USA: Compaq posts higher profits for quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: Compaq posts higher profits for quarter, year.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. Wednesday reported steeply higher profits for the fourth quarter and all of last year as its sales surged worldwide.
The world's biggest maker of personal computers said its net income for the three months ended Dec. 31 climbed to $462 million, or $1.64 a share, from $82 million, or 30 cents a share, a year ago.
Compaq's stock, which started trading about 25 minutes after the New York Stock Exchange opened, surged by $3.875 to $82.125 in heavy trading.
The company noted, however, that the 1995 fourth-quarter results included a charge of $241 million, or 87 cents a share, for purchased in-process technology acquired in acquisitions.
Compaq said its sales in the fourth quarter grew by 15 percent to $5.4 billion from $4.7 billion.

The company said its net income for all of 1996 rose to $1.3 billion, or $4.72 a share, from $789 million, or $2.88 a share. It said full-year sales grew 23 percent to $18.1 billion from $14.8 billion in 1995.
"These results reflect an excellent fourth quarter and outstanding year for Compaq," President and Chief Executive Eckhard Pfeiffer said in a statement.
"We're very pleased with the consistency of our financial progress, especially with the improvements in earnings and the growth of gross margins to 24.4 percent in the fourth quarter."
The company said an emphasis on asset management reduced its inventory by $1.0 billion and lifted its cash balance to $4.0 billion from $745 million in the previous year.
"These excellent results contributed to fourth-quarter return on invested capital of 59 percent, providing a continued increase in shareholder value," Chief Financial Officer Earl Mason said.
